title: Border and Asset
premise: Theo Marchetti, a deniable fixer for a diplomatic mission that exists on no official registry, receives a calendar invite from their handler—sent three days after the handler's body was pulled from the harbor. Following the dead man's breadcrumbs, Theo uncovers a plot to stage a catastrophic 'accident' during an upcoming summit, orchestrated from inside the very network that employs them. As Theo races the clock, they must decide whether justice served outside the law is betrayal or salvation. The story ends with Theo exposing the conspiracy at personal ruin, choosing love and truth over the institution that made them invisible.
about_author: Tamsin Ashgrove is a former policy analyst who spent a decade drafting briefings she was never allowed to sign her name to. She writes thrillers about the people history forgets on purpose.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. We meet Theo mid-extraction in Trieste, establishing their tradecraft, their polished lie of an ordinary life, and their packed bag by the door. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—the cost of being no one on purpose.

chapters.title: Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A calendar ping arrives: a meeting with handler Elias Voss, scheduled for tomorrow—three days after Voss washed up in the harbor. Theo verifies the death, then verifies the invitation is real. Beat: dread sharpening into compulsion.

chapters.title: What Voss Left Behind
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the meeting point—a shuttered tram depot—Theo finds a dead drop keyed to Voss's old cipher: a partial dossier on something called MERIDIAN and a summit date circled twice. Beat: the first vertiginous step past the edge of the map.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Counts Cameras
chapters.summary: Nadia Reyes's POV. Nadia, a summit security analyst and Theo's estranged former partner, notices surveillance blind spots being engineered around one venue. Her professional unease doubles when she spots Theo in her city. Beat: old love rekindling as suspicion.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Quietly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reports the anomaly through channels and is told, in bureaucratic language, to stand down and forget Voss. Within hours, their apartment is searched and their cover identity begins fraying. Beat: the machinery turning against its own tool.

chapters.title: Coffee with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo and Nadia meet under the pretense of coincidence; neither admits what they know. The scene crackles with unfinished history and mutual testing. Beat: intimacy as a chess game neither wants to win.

chapters.title: MERIDIAN
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Decoding Voss's files, Theo learns MERIDIAN is an internal faction monetizing the summit—an 'accident' that will kill delegates and justify a power grab. One name recurs: Deputy Director Corliss. Beat: cold clarity, hot fear.

chapters.title: The Asset Who Wouldn't Stay Bought
chapters.summary: New POV: Sable, a mercenary asset running logistics for the attack. Sable's chapter humanizes the opposition and reveals the operation's timeline: seventy-two hours. Beat: professional pride curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo goes off-grid, calculating odds: report and be disbelieved, or act alone and be branded a traitor. They choose a third path—recruit Nadia without burning her. Beat: resolve hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Bed
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Theo finally tells Nadia everything—or almost everything. Nadia, holding back her own evidence, chooses to trust anyway. The love theme crystallizes: two people choosing each other over the institutions that own them. Beat: tenderness inside danger.

chapters.title: Corliss Offers a Promotion
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Corliss summons Theo, dangles legitimacy and a real name, and makes the threat explicit: cooperate, or Nadia becomes collateral. Beat: power's corruption offered like a gift, refused like a dare.

chapters.title: The Harbor File
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia pulls port records proving Voss was murdered by a MERIDIAN wet team, and finds her own clearance quietly downgraded. She realizes she's already inside the blast radius. Beat: fear transmuted into fury.

chapters.title: Sable's Doubt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Reviewing the target package, Sable realizes the 'accident' will kill civilians, including a children's delegation—beyond any contract's fine print. Sable begins quietly sabotaging timelines. Beat: conscience waking inside a killer.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Diplomacy
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo brokers a fragile alliance with Sable through Voss's old channels, trading protection for the attack's full schematic. Beat: uneasy trust between strangers bound by a dead man's plan.

chapters.title: Seventeen Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The countdown compresses: MERIDIAN moves the operation up. Nadia works the venue's systems while Theo intercepts the trigger team's courier. A near-miss leaves Theo wounded. Beat: breathless escalation, love expressed in coordination.

chapters.title: The Trap Inside the Plan
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable discovers MERIDIAN anticipated defection—Sable's sabotage has been logged, and a second, redundant trigger exists that no one briefed Sable on. Beat: the sick drop of realizing you were always expendable.

chapters.title: Confession at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Captured by Corliss's men, Theo is given a final offer and answers with Voss's recorded confession, smuggled out via Nadia. Corliss orders Theo's execution for dawn. Beat: defiance as identity—Theo choosing the truth with a gun to their head.

chapters.title: What Nadia Does at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia trades her career's leverage—evidence implicating her own superiors in older crimes—to buy Theo's release window, then walks into the venue's control room alone. Beat: love against duty, duty losing.

chapters.title: Summit Morning
chapters.summary: Multi-POV convergence. As delegates arrive, Theo and Sable race to the redundant trigger while Nadia locks down evacuation routes. The attack launches early. Beat: every thread pulled taut, no margin left.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Climax. Theo reaches the trigger node as Sable holds off MERIDIAN's enforcers; Nadia forces the venue's fail-safes public, making concealment impossible. The device fails; the plot fails; Corliss is exposed mid-broadcast. Beat: catharsis paid for in blood—Sable falls.

chapters.title: Testimony Without a Country
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the aftermath, Theo testifies to an inquiry that wants tidy narratives, refusing to let Voss, Sable, or Nadia be erased from the record. The embassy disavows them; the truth stands anyway. Beat: justice outside the law, grief inside it.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Theo and Nadia's POV, alternating. Months later, in a coastal town under new names that are actually theirs, Theo unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years—and leaves it empty on a shelf. Beat: quiet, earned peace; visibility chosen at last.
